reason: The two quotes state the extra data transfer cost over a peering connection and the added latency and cross-region data transfer cost across Regions; the headings place them in the different-VPC sections.
The quote states that you can add a cluster to the virtual network (the VPC) and control access to it with Amazon VPC security groups.
The quote states the full copy from the primary to a new replica and the asynchronous propagation of later writes; the heading gives the cluster-mode-disabled scope.

The quotes are bare bullet items about predictable traffic and forecastable capacity; the lead-in that ties them to creating a node-based cluster ('Create your own node-based cluster if:') stands only in the surrounding text.
The quote states cluster mode with multiple shards or non-cluster mode with a single shard, under the node-based clusters text.
The quote states the choice of single-AZ or multi-AZ availability depending on needs; the heading 'Creating a node-based cluster' carries the node-based scope.
The quote states word for word that node-based clusters can be designed to provide an up to 99.99% availability SLA.
The quote states that for a node-based cluster you are responsible for choosing the type and number of nodes so the cache has enough capacity.
The table row under the Eviction Policy header states that noeviction evicts no keys and blocks future writes until memory frees up.
The quote states hourly billing from launch to termination for on-demand nodes and that each partial node-hour is billed as a full hour.
The quote states ports 11211 and 11212 for Memcached commands and that the security group must allow access to these ports.
The quote states port 6379 for node-based clusters, ports 6379 and 6380 for serverless, and that the security group must allow these ports as needed.
The quote states backup storage at $0.085 per GiB per month for all AWS Regions.
The quote states the 20% Valkey discount relative to Redis OSS and that Redis OSS reserved nodes cover 20% more running Valkey nodes with reserved node flexibility.
The quote states the $6/month start, 33% lower price on Serverless and 20% lower price on node-based compared to other supported engines.
The quote states GB-hours of data stored and ECPU compute for Serverless and per-hour node usage for node-based clusters.
The quote states the primary endpoint always resolves to the primary node and is immune to changes such as promoting a read replica.
The quote states connection over the internet without a VPC and availability on ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey 9.0 or later.
The quote states word for word that public endpoints require IAM authentication and TLS 1.3 for every connection; the heading is Serverless caching.
The quote states that caches with a public endpoint require TLS 1.3 and that TLS 1.2 and earlier are not supported for these connections.
The table row states public endpoints are supported on serverless (internet without a VPC, Valkey 9.0 or later) and not supported on node-based clusters.
The quotes are the three bullet items only; the claim's 'most effective for' clause stands only in the lead-in sentence of the surrounding text, not in any quote.

The quote follows a Valkey and Redis OSS AUTH sentence, and the next sentence limits RBAC to Valkey 7.2+ and Redis OSS 6.0 to 7.2. The claim's 'only' covers all serverless caches, Memcached included, but the quote does not carry that engine scope.

The quote states security boundaries between clients of the same Valkey or Redis OSS cache and prevention of access to each other's data; the page heading (RBAC) carries the RBAC subject of 'By doing this'.
The quote states that with AUTH all authenticated clients have full cache access and that RBAC assigns users to sets by role.
The FAQ answer under its heading states that read replicas are provisioned only in AZs of the primary's Region and that Global Datastore provides cross-Region read replica clusters.

Together the two quotes state the read-heavy, stale-tolerant nature of session stores, leaderboards and recommendation engines, and that read replicas are an effective way to reduce read latency for such use cases.
The quote states word for word that read replicas improve read throughput and guard against data loss when a node fails.
The quote states that reader endpoints work with ElastiCache (Redis OSS) clusters with cluster mode disabled.
The two quotes state the even split of incoming connections between read replicas, and that a reader endpoint is a round-robin DNS record and not a load balancer.
The quote states use of cluster-mode-disabled clusters with replicas for read-intensive applications and for many clients reading at the same time.
The quote states asynchronous replication, possible small data loss on failover due to lag, and the durability-enabled exception.
The quote states asynchronous replication to replicas, reads from any node and writes only to the primary; the heading gives the cluster-mode-disabled scope.
The quote states word for word that all nodes of a cluster-mode-disabled cluster must reside in the same Region.

The quote says 'Do not reduce this value'. The referent of 'this value', reserved-memory-percent, stands only in the preceding sentence, so the quote alone does not name the parameter the claim is about.

The quote says 'a traditional forked operation'. The claim's 'forked bgsave or full sync' comes only from the preceding sentence and the definition term. The quote supports the automatic switch, lower memory use and client latency.
The quote says only 'advertised memory minus the reserve'. The claim's 'of the host type' and 'set by reserved-memory-percent' stand only in the preceding sentences.

The quote states the database cost saving from caching frequently accessed data, and ElastiCache instead of scaling the database when read throughput needs are high.

The quote gives 30K ECPUs/second as the starting rate on an empty cache (the cache then scales; the per-cache limit is 15M), but the qualifier labels it 'max'. The claim text and the 90K Read from Replica value match.
